KSIA-ELE-001.why: DoEL registered-person certificates matched to scope; the walk names who is actually on the AGL circuits and checks their expiry.

KSIA-ELE-002.why: Approved as-builts referencing Annex 14 Ch.8; the walk confirms the designated isolation/maintenance points exist and are usable.

KSIA-ELE-003.why: An original signed CoC, not a reprint; the walk finds alterations since its date not covered by a supplementary.

KSIA-ELE-004.why: Signage present, legible and SANS 1186-1 compliant in every AGL room and outstation cabinet. Nothing documentary settles it.
KSIA-ELE-004.proof: Statutory notices and SANS 1186-1 signage present, legible and undamaged at every AGL electrical room and remote outstation cabinet, naming the CURRENT appointees and policy revision — a notice carrying a departed GMR 2(1) appointee is not a notice. Checked daily per D060 023M cl. 4.7.4, warning signage weekly, with the substation logbook signed off.

KSIA-ELE-005.why: Gaps in the daily log over weekends, and entries batched afterwards rather than signed at the time. The log's EXISTENCE is not the test.

KSIA-ELE-006.why: Measured changeover time against the Annex 14 limit for the facility's category.
gaps: the row's own question asks what the aerodrome's certified lighting category IS — the limit cannot be applied without it

KSIA-ELE-007.why: Fault log and spares register against the serviceability target; the walk counts spares against the lamp types actually in use.

KSIA-ELE-008.why: A funded plan classifying assets by criticality; the walk spot-checks older assets against what the plan says should have happened by now.

KSIA-ELE-009.why: Lamp outage within limits is settled on the runway, ideally at night.
KSIA-ELE-009.split: photometric inspection, outage limits, switch-over and CCR maintenance are four tests
KSIA-ELE-009.proof: MALMS photometric output within limits and lamp outage inside the allowed count for the pattern, the Planned AGL Maintenance Programme M&E 077 worked to date, and the secondary-power switch-over measured at 1 second for every CAT II/III element (inner 300 m approach, threshold, end, centreline, touchdown zone) on the monthly on-load test with the change-over time actually recorded.

KSIA-ELE-010.why: Route markers matching the buried route, joint boxes not paved over, accessibility to each part.
KSIA-ELE-010.proof: Cable routes to SANS 10198 with route markers present and matching the buried route, joint boxes not paved or backfilled over, the separation distances the standard requires actually measured on site, and every part reachable for inspection and replacement without dismantling something else. Commissioning test records for new MV/LV cabling and the as-built single line diagram behind it.

KSIA-ELE-011.why: The requirement is that the diagram is DISPLAYED in the room — a physical fact.
KSIA-ELE-011.split: a displayed diagram (Asset) and an applied protection grading study (Document) are different tests
KSIA-ELE-011.proof: A single-line diagram physically displayed and legible in EACH switch room, its revision date later than the most recent network change and reflecting the current Normal Open Point, plus a protection grading study whose settings an electrician can show applied in the relays — confirmed against design yearly with outage.

KSIA-ELE-012.why: Markers intact and not paved over; signs of unauthorised joints.
KSIA-ELE-012.proof: Route markers and trench covers intact, not paved over and matching the route drawing; no unrecorded joint and no sign of unmarked excavation; and the yearly thermographic scan of bus bars, breaker frames, contacts, arc-chutes and insulation blocks with every flagged hot spot carrying a closed work order.

KSIA-ELE-013.why: Compare the single-line diagram against actual breaker positions. An abnormal configuration is a state, not a record.
KSIA-ELE-013.proof: Switch and breaker positions on site matching the Normal Open Point on the single-line diagram, no equipment carrying load above its nameplate rating, and the measured values inside ACSA's stated limits — power factor at least 0.95 at the point of delivery, 50 Hz ±2.5%, MV volt drop ±5%. This is kick-off risk item 6.5.1 and an abnormal configuration left standing is the finding.

KSIA-ELE-014.why: Four certificates within 12 months per breaker, showing measured values against OEM tolerance; the walk reads the serial to prove they are THIS breaker's.

KSIA-ELE-015.why: A signed report showing actual results for all six checks, not a checklist of ticks.

KSIA-ELE-016.why: Condition assessment and a capital plan entry; the walk reads the nameplate date and looks for degraded condition.

KSIA-ELE-017.why: 'Available AND USED' is the requirement. Tests whether the register is maintained when someone leaves and whether LOTO is actually applied.
KSIA-ELE-017.split: switching authority (Practice) and arc-flash PPE condition (Asset) in one row

KSIA-ELE-018.why: Rooms physically separate, each with its own access control rather than a shared key across risk classes.
KSIA-ELE-018.proof: MV breaker, transformer, LV, generator and battery/UPS rooms each physically separate, each with its own access control rather than a shared key across risk classes, each containing only its designated equipment, oil-filled units with containment and fire-sealed penetrations. NOTE: ACSA states no numeric fire rating and no bund percentage for these rooms, so the compliance test is separation and containment as built, against the layout drawing.

KSIA-ELE-019.why: Ventilation actually running rather than merely installed; rodent and corrosion free; drainage present.

KSIA-ELE-020.why: Measure the clearance around switchgear and busbars against the NRS 060 table. A tape measure decides it.
KSIA-ELE-020.proof: Clearance around MV/LV switchgear and busbars measured on site and at or above the NRS 060 figure for the installed voltage class, no storage or clutter inside it, doors serviceable, lockable and unobstructed, and exactly one door or gate left unlocked for emergency egress while work is in progress.

KSIA-ELE-021.why: A plan that references the actual rooms on site rather than a generic site-wide document, plus drill records.

KSIA-ELE-022.why: Displayed at all times, legible, revision-dated. A physical fact about a wall.
KSIA-ELE-022.proof: The latest revision of the substation diagram displayed, legible, dated and revision-numbered, reflecting the current Normal Open Point, and matching the switching configuration found during the walkdown. Inspected daily with corrective action raised where it is out of date.

KSIA-ELE-023.why: Door not propped open, signage legible, HVAC running, no unrelated storage.
KSIA-ELE-023.proof: Door access-controlled and not propped, keys issued through the key register with receipt on return, statutory signage present and legible, ventilation actually running, no unrelated storage, and MV/LV/UPS/CCR separated where practical — with the substation logbook showing all sixteen daily checks signed off.

KSIA-ELE-024.why: Thermography, earthing resistance and oil test reports within period; the walk looks for discolouration and melted insulation.
KSIA-ELE-024.proof: Thermographic survey within the year with every hot spot closed out; earth resistance measured and recorded at the yearly transformer major maintenance; and transformer oil DGA/BDV within period with PCB content not more than 20 mg/kg in reclaimed oil and undetectable in unused oil, determined per IEC 61619 to SANS 555. NOTE: ACSA states no numeric earth resistance value, so the test is that a measured figure exists and is trended, against the design value.

KSIA-ELE-025.why: The question is decisive: a complete log of tests that were START-AND-IDLE rather than ON-LOAD is a complete record of the wrong test.

KSIA-ELE-026.why: A pressure/leak integrity certificate for the underground pipework.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether leak detection is by actual pressure test or only consumption reconciliation — those are different assurances

KSIA-ELE-027.why: Signage present and legible in the zones the assessment identifies, specifying the right protection.

KSIA-ELE-028.why: MHI declaration or written confirmation of being below threshold; the walk confirms the tank capacity matches the volume assessed.

KSIA-ELE-029.why: Whether staff entering the generator room during operation ACTUALLY wear the issued protection. Issue records prove issue, not use.

KSIA-ELE-030.why: The cut-out and e-stop located, labelled, unobstructed. A March 2025 Unacceptable finding sat here.
KSIA-ELE-030.proof: A fuel cut-out or isolation device and an emergency stop at each generator, both clearly labelled, unobstructed and reachable WITHOUT approaching the generator itself, with the fuel line shut-off valve checked to operate freely weekly and the stop solenoid checked on the monthly record.

KSIA-ELE-031.why: Weekly/monthly entries without gaps and an annual load-bank test; the walk compares the hour-meter to what is logged.
KSIA-ELE-031.proof: Weekly off-load runs of at least five minutes and monthly on-load runs of at least fifteen minutes, with no gaps in the logbook, the hour-meter reading consistent with what is logged, the change-over time recorded on each on-load test, and an annual load-bank test plus fuel sample analysis for every generator — not just the main one.

KSIA-ELE-032.why: ATS test records showing switch-over within design; the walk finds a recent test or service tag on the cabinet.
KSIA-ELE-032.proof: A tested ATS with the measured change-over time at or under the design figure for the load it feeds — 1 second for every CAT II/III AGL element. A test record with no time on it does not answer this check.

KSIA-ELE-033.why: Bund cracked or full of rainwater, spill kit missing, visible leaks.
KSIA-ELE-033.split: bund condition and alarms (Asset) vs fuel quality tests (Document)
KSIA-ELE-033.proof: Bund intact, not cracked and not full of rainwater (which is capacity gone), sized to at least 110% of the largest container, level alarms proven on the weekly alarm check, a stocked and accessible spill kit, no leaks or staining, and the annual bulk-tank bottom and primary-filter samples analysed for contamination.

KSIA-ELE-034.why: Current-year oil report with prior years for trending.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether DGA was actually done or only basic tests — a different assurance

KSIA-ELE-035.why: Oil level, leaks and staining, silica gel colour, bushings, cooling fins. All read at the transformer.
KSIA-ELE-035.proof: Oil level in band with no leaks or staining, silica gel the right colour, bushings and cooling fins undamaged and clean, Buchholz and temperature protection warning and trip functionality tested at the yearly major maintenance with outage, and the measured loading inside the nameplate rating.

KSIA-ELE-036.why: Impedance/capacity and discharge test certificates — a discharge test is verified by certificate, not observed; the walk looks for swelling, leakage, corrosion.
KSIA-ELE-036.proof: Battery impedance or capacity results and a full-duration autonomy discharge test within period, alarms proven to reach the monitoring point, and the UPS room temperature inside the battery manufacturer's specification — recorded on the annual service alongside cell readings, charger voltage, inverter output and the bypass switch test.

KSIA-ELE-037.why: The flight-check report itself, within the facility's interval — not ground maintenance records standing in for it.

KSIA-ELE-038.why: Each parameter against the Annex 10 tolerance table for the facility's category.

KSIA-ELE-039.why: Calibration certificates per sensor within validity; the walk reads each sensor's tag date against its certificate.

KSIA-ELE-040.why: A lux survey measured at the actual task points, within the two-year re-survey interval.

KSIA-ELE-041.why: Dark or uneven apron areas at night, and high-mast base/foundation condition.
KSIA-ELE-041.proof: Measured lux readings on the specified grid at or above 20 LUX per ICAO Annex 14 §5.3.24, taken monthly, with uniformity across the apron rather than an average that hides a dark stand; high-mast structures and foundations inspected for corrosion and cracking; landside and parking lighting operational.

KSIA-ELE-042.why: Monthly function and annual full-duration tests logged; the walk actually isolates a fitting to see it switch on.
KSIA-ELE-042.proof: Monthly function tests and an annual full-duration test logged per fitting, six-monthly integrity testing of the back-up supply with a light output measurement, daily escape-route clearance checks, and fittings found undamaged and unobstructed on the walk.

KSIA-ELE-043.why: Service certificates and quarterly test logs; the walk reads the panel for faults and the cylinder gauges.
KSIA-ELE-043.split: detection servicing, suppression cylinder checks and room-integrity testing are three tests
KSIA-ELE-043.proof: Fire detection inspected weekly and maintained monthly with the panel showing no standing fault, quarterly functional tests logged, gas suppression maintained yearly with each cylinder's weight, gas type, inspection date and next service recorded, cylinders within their 10-yearly hydrostatic test, and a room-integrity (door fan) test proving the enclosure will hold the concentration.

KSIA-ELE-044.why: Licence current and matching the machine's serial; RPO appointed.
KSIA-ELE-044.proof: Current Department of Health radiation registration verified annually and matching each machine's serial number, an appointed Radiation Protection Officer whom staff can name and whose appointment record matches, tri-monthly leakage survey and calibration certificates, and deregistration records for any machine removed.

KSIA-ELE-045.why: Test certificates within period; the walk checks bonding cables at a fuelling point are intact and not corroded or disconnected.
KSIA-ELE-045.proof: Earth resistance and lightning-protection test certificates within period, and bonding at airside structures and fuelling points physically intact, uncorroded and connected with a test tag showing a recent date. NOTE: ACSA states no numeric ohm value, so the test is a measured figure against the design value and its trend — not the absence of one.

KSIA-ELE-046.why: Training records and DoEL registration; the walk asks staff what training they had and cross-checks the register.

KSIA-ELE-047.why: As-builts and CoCs referencing the SANS 10142-1 edition current when the work was done; the walk finds undocumented changes.

KSIA-ELE-048.why: Notices present, legible, not faded or damaged, at each electrical room and work point.
KSIA-ELE-048.proof: As ELE-004, across every general electrical room and work point: statutory notices, SANS 1186-1 signage, circuit labels and legend cards present, legible and current, checked daily, warning signs and safety devices confirmed present and correctly positioned.

KSIA-ELE-049.why: As ELE-005 for the general installation: gaps in the log and batched sign-off are the finding.

KSIA-ELE-050.why: Enclosure panels left open or unlocked after maintenance; barrier voltage ratings against the installed class.

KSIA-ELE-051.why: The question is the test — is LOTO bypassed 'for a quick job'. Lockable isolators existing is necessary and not sufficient.

KSIA-ELE-052.why: Whether each SWMS is specific to the job's hazards or one generic document reused. A file full of identical SWMSs passes a document test and fails this one.

KSIA-ELE-053.why: A current GMR 2.1 appointment naming someone still on the roster, plus a dated functional test log.

KSIA-ELE-054.why: Guards fitted over rotating parts and live terminals, not removed or propped open.

KSIA-MEC-001.why: A measured L/s per person on a dated test report. The walk only proves the fan is running and that the space is the space that was tested.
gaps: ACSA requires only a six-monthly MOTOR RUNNING CURRENT — no air-flow rate, velocity or L/s figure anywhere in D080 025M. The check asks for a test ACSA's own manual does not call for.
KSIA-MEC-001.proof: Independent air-flow test for the space, measured fresh-air rate against the >7.5 L/s/person target, with the space classified as it is actually used — an office re-let as a concourse invalidates the report.

KSIA-MEC-002.why: Air changes per hour is a calculation from a measured extract rate and the room's real volume. Neither is visible.
gaps: ACSA states no extraction rate or air-change requirement — only motor running current
KSIA-MEC-002.proof: ACH report with the room volume used, the measured extract flow, and the calculated ACH — with the volume matching the actual room.

KSIA-MEC-003.why: The required extraction rate comes from the fire engineering design; only a commissioning certificate can show the fan achieves it.
gaps: ACSA's threshold is a 3-monthly auxiliary activation test, not a flow rate
KSIA-MEC-003.proof: Approved smoke control design stating the rate for the zone, plus a functional test certificate showing the fan reached it when triggered BY the fire alarm, not standalone.

KSIA-MEC-004.why: Grease depth in a duct is the fact, and it is behind an access panel. The certificate says the run was cleaned; the panel says whether it was cleaned end to end.
KSIA-MEC-004.proof: Deep-clean certificate per SANS 1850:2003 at an interval not exceeding six months, with before/after photographs or a deposit-depth reading covering the full duct run to the discharge point.

KSIA-MEC-005.why: A seized vent is visible on the roof, but what fails this check is a blanket 'all vents OK' sign-off with no per-unit entry.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — no monthly roof-vent test interval is stated anywhere in the source
KSIA-MEC-005.proof: Monthly log with a per-unit reference and pass/fail, and a roof sample turning freely without seizure or corrosion.

KSIA-MEC-006.why: A damper closes or it does not, and only a functional test says so. The walk finds the ones painted over or sealed above a ceiling.
KSIA-MEC-006.proof: Test record per damper reference showing full closure and reset, cross-referenced to the fire safety file — and a located sample with its access panel still openable and the blade not painted shut.

KSIA-MEC-007.why: A Certificate of Conformity under PER reg 17 is the only proof. The walk matches the plant-room reference on it to the pipework actually installed.
KSIA-MEC-007.proof: Current CoC from an Approved Inspection Authority, and no unrecorded modification — new branches or welds — since its date.

KSIA-MEC-008.why: A Legionella result is a laboratory number. The walk exists to count towers, because a certificate for one tower on a site with three is the failure.
gaps: no acsaThreshold at all — SANS 10147 cl. 6.1.6.1 is named in the evidence but no ACSA interval is quoted
KSIA-MEC-008.proof: A dated clearance certificate within 12 months for EACH water-cooled or evaporative system, with sampling points that match the plant on site.

KSIA-MEC-009.why: An EIR reg 6 Certificate of Compliance signed by a registered person. The walk looks for circuits added since.
KSIA-MEC-009.proof: Current CoC in the latest SANS 10142-1 format naming the registered person, matching the as-installed wiring with no un-certified additions.

KSIA-MEC-010.why: A drawing is compliant when it matches the installation, which is only knowable by tracing circuits against it.
KSIA-MEC-010.proof: Dated, version-controlled as-built set — 1 electronic and 3 hard copies per D100MAN cl. 9.2 — with panel labelling in the plant room matching it, not the original design issue never updated.

KSIA-MEC-011.why: An interface test is a record of a response that has already happened. What matters is whether the HVAC plant moved, or only the fire panel logged.
KSIA-MEC-011.proof: Quarterly record showing the alarm triggered and the HVAC response observed, cross-referenced to a cause-and-effect matrix covering every interface zone.

KSIA-MEC-012.why: The trip current and time are on a drawing and in a test record. The walk reads the installed device's rating and looks for a bypass.
gaps: no standalone earth-leakage test interval in ACSA — it rides on the yearly COC cycle
this identical check appears six times in the register: MEC-012, 052, 064, 087, 092, 102
KSIA-MEC-012.split: one earth-leakage check scoped by asset system, not six near-identical rows

KSIA-MEC-013.why: A leak check is an event with a method. Repeated top-ups with no investigated cause is the finding, and it is only visible in the log.
KSIA-MEC-013.proof: Quarterly leak-check record per refrigerant circuit stating the detection method used and referenced to the charge, with any detected leak repaired and verified.

KSIA-MEC-014.why: A laboratory report from the Environmental department against stated guideline values. Nothing on site changes it.
gaps: no walkabout text at all, correctly
KSIA-MEC-014.proof: IAQ report within the two-year Occupational Hygiene cycle, naming the reference standard it was assessed against.

KSIA-MEC-015.why: An audit report and its recommendations. The walk spot-checks whether a named finding was actually actioned.
KSIA-MEC-015.proof: Annual energy optimisation report for the HVAC plant, and for each cited finding either a closed work order or the unit visibly in the state the recommendation called for.

KSIA-MEC-016.why: A SANS 10083 noise assessment by an Approved Inspection Authority. The walk checks the zones it named are demarcated on the ground.
gaps: verbatim duplicate of MEC-105 — same requirement, evidence and walkabout, one filed under HVAC and one under Water Treatment Plant
KSIA-MEC-016.split: one noise-survey check for the site; demarcation is separately MEC-104

KSIA-MEC-017.why: Weekly logged temperatures, pressures and amps against set-points. AUTO mode and an unacknowledged alarm are read off the BMS screen.
gaps: overlaps MEC-007 (PER certificates) and MEC-013 (refrigerant leak log)
KSIA-MEC-017.split: keep the plant-log half; the PER certificate is MEC-007 and the leak log is MEC-013
KSIA-MEC-017.proof: Weekly chiller records of temperature, pressure and amps with the delta-T against design, controller in AUTO with no standing alarm, yearly oil sample analysis and the safety-device test.

KSIA-MEC-018.why: The dosing regime and its test results decide it — but biological growth in the basin is visible and contradicts a clean record.
gaps: overlaps MEC-008, whose evidence is the same Legionella certificates
KSIA-MEC-018.split: keep the water-treatment programme and cleaning records here; Legionella testing is MEC-008
KSIA-MEC-018.proof: A documented water treatment programme with dosing pumps and chemical tanks connected and charged (not empty or disconnected), cleaning and disinfection records, monthly leak/eliminator/fan/spray inspection and tri-monthly sump cleaning per the Cooling Towers checklist CMMS 009 — and a basin and fill free of visible biological growth, which contradicts a clean record.

KSIA-MEC-019.why: An Annexure A is issued once, after erection. The walk matches the serial plate to the certificate and looks for a controller change that voids it.
KSIA-MEC-019.proof: Annexure A per lift referencing SANS 1545-1 or 1545-2, with a fresh one after any substantial modification.

KSIA-MEC-020.why: A two-yearly thorough examination report with a next-due date. The walk's job is counting — every lift in a bank, not most of them.
KSIA-MEC-020.proof: Annexure B per lift dated within 24 months, examiner's registration stated, next-due date not yet passed.

KSIA-MEC-021.why: As MEC-019, for escalators and conveyors against SANS 1543.
gaps: ACSA's threshold here is a MONTHLY check of the reports, which is a different obligation from holding a valid Annexure A

KSIA-MEC-022.why: As MEC-020, for the escalator and conveyor fleet.
KSIA-MEC-022.proof: Annexure B per unit dated within 24 months across the whole fleet, next-due date not passed.

KSIA-MEC-023.why: A SANS 1545-3 certificate per stairlift. The walk finds the unit installed in an accessibility upgrade that nobody certificated.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — platform stairlifts are not in D080 020M's inspection tables at all

KSIA-MEC-024.why: An Annexure E must address accessibility features. A generic Annexure B filed under this heading is the failure, and only reading it shows that.
KSIA-MEC-024.proof: Current Annexure E addressing audible and tactile controls, door timing, alarm button at 900-1200 mm and a mirror where the car is under 1 500 mm wide.

KSIA-MEC-025.why: Rope discard criteria are applied by a competent person against a specific rope set. Visible corrosion in the hoistway supports or contradicts the report.
KSIA-MEC-025.proof: Six-monthly examination naming the specific rope set, assessed against discard criteria, with the certificate in its designated place in the machine compartment and retained ten years.

KSIA-MEC-026.why: A destructive test that has already happened; the report is all there is. What it must show is a measured trip speed, and all three elements tested.
KSIA-MEC-026.proof: Annual report per lift confirming safety gear engaged, the governor tripped at a measured speed with units stated, and the buffers tested — not the governor alone.

KSIA-MEC-027.why: As MEC-009, for the lift motor room supply and control panel.
gaps: duplicates the CoC pattern of MEC-009, 031, 052, 064, 089, 094, 101

KSIA-MEC-028.why: A roll-up of the certificate checks above, adding one thing they miss: whether the register lists every unit in the terminal.
KSIA-MEC-028.split: keep only the register completeness and the displayed-certificate check — walk the terminal, count the units, reconcile against the register
KSIA-MEC-028.proof: A register listing every lift, escalator and travelator in the terminal, reconciled by walking it; a current comprehensive report per unit to SANS 1545-1:2016 ed 3.6 at the two-yearly cycle or on contractor change; the Appointed Inspector's appointment letter; and the certificate displayed at each unit current and matching that unit's ID. Records retained ten years.

KSIA-MEC-029.why: The one People Movers check decided entirely on the machine. A broken comb tooth and a cracked handrail are seen and felt, and no certificate discloses them.
KSIA-MEC-029.proof: Step/pallet-to-skirt gaps within tolerance, no two adjacent comb teeth broken, handrails uncracked and un-frayed, landing plates secure, skirt brushes fitted, emergency stops present and unobstructed, signage legible.

KSIA-MEC-030.why: Four safety systems, each with its own OEM test. The record must show all four were exercised — the easy ones alone is the common failure.
KSIA-MEC-030.proof: OEM functional test at the FALE four-monthly cycle covering auto-levelling, bumper/obstruction sensors, emergency stop and cabin interlock.

KSIA-MEC-031.why: As MEC-009, for the bridge's supply and control installation, matched to the gate number.
gaps: requirement is one word, 'COC' — no scope, no interval, no issuing authority stated in the check itself

KSIA-MEC-032.why: Welds, bogies and undercarriage corrosion are assessed by a competent person with access the auditor does not have. The report's SCOPE is the check.
gaps: conflicting intervals in the source: FALE's own cycle is 2-yearly in years 2 and 4, against a counter-benchmark of a three-monthly visual structural inspection
KSIA-MEC-032.proof: Two-yearly report explicitly covering welds, support structure, wheel bogies/undercarriage and corrosion — not only the visible cabin structure.

KSIA-MEC-033.why: A PrEng structural assessment is a professional opinion in a report.
gaps: ACSA's own manual requires NO such report — the register's acsaEvidence field says '(none required by D080 029M)'. The check demands evidence ACSA does not oblige anyone to hold.
KSIA-MEC-033.split: merge into MEC-032, and raise the missing PrEng requirement as a policy gap against ACSA rather than as a site non-compliance
KSIA-MEC-033.proof: A structural assessment report by an ECSA-registered Professional Engineer covering corrosion, welds, rotunda, tunnel and wheel bogie, with every remedial action closed. NOTE: ACSA's D080 029M requires no such report — treat a missing one as a gap in ACSA's manual to be raised, and demand instead the counter-benchmark D080 028M cl. 4.2.5 six-monthly/yearly structural inspection by a competent person.

KSIA-MEC-034.why: Auto-leveller, safety shoe, canopy and emergency stop are demonstrated on the bridge by an operator. That demonstration, not the PM sheet, is what settles it.
gaps: overlaps MEC-030, which tests the same four systems from the record side
KSIA-MEC-034.split: keep the demonstration here; the OEM test record is MEC-030; the operator authorisation register is a Document check of its own
KSIA-MEC-034.proof: The auto-leveller demonstrated adjusting, the safety shoe present and moving freely, the canopy undamaged and without gaps, drive/steer working and the emergency stop located and functional — plus the four-monthly FALE task tables completed, faults carrying an IMC reference number, and an operator authorisation register naming everyone who drives the bridge.

KSIA-MEC-035.why: An MHIR reg 5 risk assessment by an Approved Inspection Authority, five-yearly. The walk checks the fuel farm has not outgrown what it covers.
KSIA-MEC-035.proof: Current AIA MHI risk assessment within 5 years, proof of submission to the Chief Inspector, local and provincial government, and a tank/hydrant configuration matching what it assessed.

KSIA-MEC-036.why: The plan is a document; whether it was drilled is a record of an event. The walk checks the plan still describes the site it is for.
gaps: requirement says 3-yearly but ACSA requires the plan TESTED at least every 12 months and SUBMITTED to NERSA annually — three different clocks in one check
KSIA-MEC-036.split: split in two — the plan's currency and consultation with the local authority (Document), and the annual practical drill (Practice)

KSIA-MEC-037.why: A witnessed pressure test certificate. The AIA's stamp is the point — a contractor's own sign-off is not the same document.
gaps: DIRECT CONFLICT: the check says 3-yearly, ACSA D060 021M cl. 4.17.5 says the hydrant line pressure test at FALE (King Shaka) is YEARLY. Auditing FALE against 3 years would pass an installation that is two years overdue.
KSIA-MEC-037.proof: AIA-witnessed certificate within ONE year for FALE, stating test pressure and result, covering the tank farm AND the hydrant lines.

KSIA-MEC-038.why: A design package and its certification. The walk spot-checks material spec plates against it and finds the older sections nobody has documentation for.
gaps: CONFLICTING CODE: the check names ASME B31.3; ACSA D060 021M cl. 4.15.1 names API/IP 1540 plus JIG. No wall-thickness or design criterion is stated for either.
KSIA-MEC-038.proof: Piping design package certified to the code ACSA actually adopts, plus the Petroleum Pipeline Act construction licence, with documentation covering every section including the oldest.

KSIA-MEC-039.why: A calibration certificate against a serial number. The walk exists to catch a bump test recorded as a calibration, which is the routine substitution here.
gaps: 'potable gas meters' — almost certainly PORTABLE gas meters; the register carries the typo
ACSA names four calibration items (crawl beams, gauges, hydrocarbon detectors, tightness control system) and NO quarterly interval
KSIA-MEC-039.proof: Full calibration certificate — not a bump test — from a competent provider, referencing the meter serial number found on the instrument.

KSIA-MEC-040.why: The record must show fuel flow actually stopped, not that a button was pressed. The walk confirms staff know what the button isolates.
gaps: ACSA does not define 'ESB'; the manual's term is ESD, maintained six-monthly at FALE. The check and the manual may not be describing the same device.
KSIA-MEC-040.proof: Functional test showing the valve or pump actually isolated, plus the approved Safe Work Procedure for emergency fuel hydrant shut-off signed by the GMR 2(1) and 2(7) appointees.

KSIA-MEC-041.why: An as-built is compliant only against the tank farm it claims to describe. That comparison is the whole check.
KSIA-MEC-041.proof: Version-controlled as-built set in PDF and native format, named by project/drawing/revision, minimum A3, with no tank, valve or hydrant on site missing from it and none on it missing from site.

KSIA-MEC-042.why: Pipe-to-soil potential is a millivolt reading against a criterion. Only the log has it; the walk confirms the rectifier is actually being read.
gaps: the -850 mV CSE criterion is in the check's evidence but nowhere in ACSA's threshold — ACSA states intervals only
KSIA-MEC-042.proof: Readings at the site's stated interval, each identifying the pipe section or tank it relates to, against -850 mV CSE, with a linked work order for any out-of-range reading.

KSIA-MEC-043.why: Buried coating can only be seen during an excavation or inferred from a close-interval survey. On a normal audit there is nothing to look at.
gaps: no coating inspection interval and no holiday-test criterion in ACSA
the check may be unanswerable in an audit period with no excavation — it needs an explicit 'not applicable this period' outcome rather than a fail
KSIA-MEC-043.proof: Coating-integrity records from any excavation in the period, or a close-interval survey — and where neither exists, that stated as the reason rather than left blank.

KSIA-MEC-044.why: You open the pit and look in. Water ingress, a failed seal and an unrated fitting are all read on the spot.
gaps: duplicates MEC-046 (lids) and MEC-054 (couplers, seals, lids, water)
KSIA-MEC-044.proof: Pit box and chamber intact, draining, sealed, with any electrical equipment inside rated for its hazardous-area zone.

KSIA-MEC-045.why: Leak-tightness is a measured rate. The walk counts pit valves against the records, because partial coverage is the usual state.
gaps: ACSA notes 'leak rate is to be noted but NO numeric limit' — the check has no pass mark to test against
KSIA-MEC-045.proof: A test record for EVERY pit valve, and the maintenance manual it references actually existing on site with a stated frequency.

KSIA-MEC-046.why: Corrosion, a perished seal and a lid that will not close are seen on the apron, and each is a trip or FOD hazard in its own right.
gaps: no acsaThreshold for anodising, seal condition or lid functionality — daily inspection is required but no criterion is given
KSIA-MEC-046.split: one hydrant pit condition check covering box, chamber, lid, seals and couplers

KSIA-MEC-047.why: The distinction between a dynamic and a static test is only visible in how the record describes the conditions. Nothing on the apron tells you which was done.
gaps: no acsaThreshold at all for a dynamic closing test
KSIA-MEC-047.proof: A record describing an under-flow closing test with the flow condition stated, and a linked corrective action for any valve that failed to seal.

KSIA-MEC-048.why: Meter proving is a metrological certificate against a serial number, and the walk exists to find the meter that has none.
gaps: ACSA's calibration list names Gauges but not custody-transfer meter proving; no annual proving interval is stated
KSIA-MEC-048.proof: Current proving certificate for EVERY dispensing or custody-transfer meter, with the NRCS verification where applicable, and an out-of-tolerance result followed by adjustment and re-prove.

KSIA-MEC-049.why: An internal inspection happens inside an emptied tank. The report and its calculated next-due date are the only access an auditor has.
gaps: API 653 is named in the check's evidence but not by ACSA — ACSA requires five-yearly CLEANING, which is a different operation from an integrity inspection
KSIA-MEC-049.proof: Inspection report with bottom-plate thickness readings and a calculated remaining life or next-due date, and no external shell staining that contradicts it.

KSIA-MEC-050.why: A zone map is a drawing. It is compliant when it matches the plant, and the way to test that is to stand in a zone and read an equipment rating.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — SANS 10108 is named only in the check's own evidence field
KSIA-MEC-050.proof: Current zone classification drawing reflecting the plant as it now stands, with field equipment carrying at least the Ex rating its zone requires.

KSIA-MEC-051.why: SANS 10086 inspection grades are recorded, not observed. The walk samples glands and enclosures and checks the register covers what is installed.
gaps: overlaps MEC-053, which reads the same nameplates for the same zones
KSIA-MEC-051.split: keep the periodic inspection regime here; the Ex-certification of machinery is MEC-053

KSIA-MEC-052.why: Three separate checks — earth leakage, wiring diagram, CoC — bundled into one row for the fuel system.
gaps: three checks in one requirement, each already asked separately elsewhere
duplicates MEC-012, MEC-010 and MEC-009 respectively
KSIA-MEC-052.split: split three ways, or scope the single earth-leakage, diagram and CoC checks by asset system

KSIA-MEC-053.why: An Ex mark is stamped on a nameplate you can read with a torch. Under-rated equipment in a Zone 1 is found by looking, not by reading a file.
KSIA-MEC-053.proof: Every machine in a hazardous zone carrying a valid Ex mark rated at or above its zone, cross-checked against SANS 10089-2 and the zone map.

KSIA-MEC-054.why: Couplers, seals, lids and standing water are all read by opening a pit.
gaps: evidence stub: 'Pit inspection register; site walk'
KSIA-MEC-054.split: merge MEC-044, 046 and 054 into one hydrant pit condition check
KSIA-MEC-054.proof: Couplers undamaged, seals not cracked or perished, lids seating securely, no standing water or fuel in the pit by eye or smell, the weekly FALE fuel-on-water-table test done, daily inspection and cleaning records, and a pit valve and lid register covering every pit on the apron rather than a sample.

KSIA-MEC-055.why: Pressure, tightness and ESD tests are all records; bonding continuity is a measured resistance.
gaps: duplicates MEC-037 (pressure test), MEC-040 (ESD) and MEC-045 (tightness)
bonding at fuelling positions appears nowhere else and has no ACSA threshold — it is the only new content in the row
KSIA-MEC-055.split: delete the duplicated halves; keep bonding at fuelling positions as its own check
KSIA-MEC-055.proof: The FALE hydrant line statutory pressure test within ONE year (not three), tightness control system maintained monthly with the leak rate noted, ESD maintained six-monthly with the push-buttons found unobstructed, clearly marked and undamaged at every fuelling position, and bonding continuity at fuelling positions measured — plus the approved Safe Work Procedure for emergency hydrant shut-off.

KSIA-MEC-056.why: A bund wall crack, a blocked bund drain and a corroded tank shell are all seen. The product-quality records bundled in are not.
gaps: four unrelated things in one row: tank inspection, bund integrity, filter/separator maintenance, product quality
KSIA-MEC-056.split: split the bund and filter condition (Asset) from tank integrity (MEC-049) and product quality records (Document)
KSIA-MEC-056.proof: External inspection tag on each tank current, shell and roof free of corrosion, coating failure and leaks; bund wall uncracked, dry and drain valve closed; five-yearly tank cleaning and ten-yearly flood survey records; weekly fuel filter and separator pit maintenance; a current Fuel Depot Licence; and product quality records for each grade.

KSIA-MEC-057.why: You trip an interlock and the conveyor stops, or it does not. A defeated interlock is the finding and it is only visible at the machine.
KSIA-MEC-057.proof: Interlock trip observed stopping the belt, siren sounding before start-up on the monthly cycle, and no interlock bridged, taped or bypassed for throughput.

KSIA-MEC-058.why: A missing nip-point guard is seen from the walkway. No record substitutes for that.
gaps: overlaps MEC-057, MEC-062 and MEC-065 — four checks walking the same conveyor guarding
KSIA-MEC-058.proof: Every identified nip point guarded, guards intact and reinstated after maintenance, and no interlock switch on a guard bridged out.

KSIA-MEC-059.why: Whether a siren is audible over terminal noise, and whether it precedes motion by a real margin, has to be heard.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — no siren duration or margin before motion is stated anywhere
KSIA-MEC-059.proof: Siren heard above ambient terminal noise, sounding with a stated margin before the carousel moves — and a documented required duration to measure that margin against.

KSIA-MEC-060.why: An E-stop is pressed and the line halts with no auto-restart. Damage and obstruction are seen at the same time.
KSIA-MEC-060.proof: Sample of E-stops physically tested, immediate halt with deliberate manual reset, none damaged or obstructed.

KSIA-MEC-061.why: What matters is whether the shutter was triggered BY the fire alarm or closed by hand and written up as if triggered. Only the record and the cause-and-effect matrix show that.
KSIA-MEC-061.proof: Test records for both directions — closure on fire alarm and the carousel interlock — cross-referenced to a cause-and-effect matrix held on site.

KSIA-MEC-062.why: Same physical test as MEC-057, across the sortation system.
KSIA-MEC-062.split: merge into MEC-057, scoped to cover every interlock zone rather than a sample

KSIA-MEC-063.why: Same audible test as MEC-059, on the sorter.
KSIA-MEC-063.split: one siren check covering carousel and sorter

KSIA-MEC-064.why: Two checks in one, both already asked elsewhere, scoped to the BHS control DBs.
gaps: duplicates MEC-012 (earth leakage) and MEC-010 (wiring diagrams and CoC)

KSIA-MEC-065.why: Guards and E-stops are the physical half and already covered above. Lock-out is a procedure and spares holding is a stores record — neither is a condition.
gaps: three different check types in one row
KSIA-MEC-065.split: split three ways — guarding and E-stops (already MEC-057/058/060), lock-out/tag-out procedure and its records (Practice), critical drive spares holding (Document)
KSIA-MEC-065.proof: Guards fitted over every moving part, drive unit and pinch point with none missing, propped or bypassed; E-stops present, reachable and unobstructed along the route; a documented lock-out/tag-out procedure with records of its use; PM scheduled at least thirty days ahead with deviation admin closed within one workday; and critical drive spares held at the minimum quantity (annual usage / 12 months) on the KARDEX card.

KSIA-MEC-066.why: The hydrostatic test date is stamped on the cylinder. You read it off the extinguisher standing in front of you.
KSIA-MEC-066.proof: Legible test stamp on each cylinder within the SANS 1475-1 interval for its TYPE — CO2 read against the CO2 table, not the water/foam one.

KSIA-MEC-067.why: In its logged location, gauge in the green, pin and seal intact, undamaged — every element is read on the unit.
gaps: ACSA requires inspection QUARTERLY; the check's evidence asks for a MONTHLY visual log — two different intervals in one check
KSIA-MEC-067.proof: Extinguisher present where the register says, accessible, needle in the green, seal and pin intact, no damage — and the inspection log without gaps.

KSIA-MEC-068.why: A roll-up of MEC-066 and MEC-067 with one addition: whether the type and location match the fire hazard class of the area.
KSIA-MEC-068.split: keep only 'correct type and location for the area's fire hazard class', which nothing else asks, and reconcile it against MEC-069
KSIA-MEC-068.proof: Service tag on each extinguisher showing an annual service within twelve months by a SANS 1475-accredited provider with the provider named; the hydrostatic date stamped on the cylinder within the retest interval FOR ITS TYPE; inspection tags with no gap in the quarterly cycle; and the type and size at each location matching the area's SANS 10400-T fire hazard class.

KSIA-MEC-069.why: A SANS 10400-T classification per occupancy. It fails when an area's actual use has moved on from the class it carries — which is a walk, not a read.
KSIA-MEC-069.proof: A classification record covering every occupancy, and each area's current use still matching its assigned fire load — an office turned into a store is the failure.

KSIA-MEC-070.why: A block plan is only useful at the valve station in an emergency. Held centrally, it fails the purpose even if it exists.
KSIA-MEC-070.proof: A physical copy of the SANS 10287 block plan at each valve station, with valve numbering matching the tags in the field.

KSIA-MEC-071.why: A flow and pressure figure is the test. A visual 'hose OK' recorded as a test is the failure, and only the record discloses it.
KSIA-MEC-071.proof: SANS 10105-2 record showing an actual flow/pressure check against design flow, hose and nozzle condition, isolating valve free — plus SANS 1475-2 reconditioning certificates for any reel sent away.

KSIA-MEC-072.why: Measured L/s and residual bar, compared against the fire-engineering design values. The comparison is the check — a recorded number with nothing to compare it to proves nothing.
KSIA-MEC-072.proof: Annual test per hydrant with measured flow and residual pressure explicitly compared to the design report, and the hydrant free and not leaking at the gland.

KSIA-MEC-073.why: A painted-over head, stock stacked into the spray pattern and a corroded rosette are all seen from below.
KSIA-MEC-073.proof: Heads unpainted, unobstructed, uncorroded, correctly oriented — and an inspection record itemised by zone rather than a sitewide sign-off.

KSIA-MEC-074.why: Thirty seconds is a measured elapsed time on a log. The walk can watch one test, but the weekly series is the compliance.
KSIA-MEC-074.proof: Weekly log per valve station recording the elapsed time to alarm against the 30-second target, and the signal reaching the monitored fire control room — not just a local sounder.

KSIA-MEC-075.why: A service record from an ASIB-registered or insurer-approved provider, identifying which valve of which zone.
gaps: CONFLICT: the check says 3-yearly, ACSA D080 002M cl. 4.7.8 says deluge/control valve service records YEARLY
KSIA-MEC-075.proof: Service record at the interval ACSA actually requires, naming the specific valves serviced across every deluge zone.

KSIA-MEC-076.why: An ASIB Certificate of Inspection. Its coverage is the question — a multi-building network partly certificated reads as compliant until you compare.
gaps: ACSA qualifies this '(if applicable)' and never says when it applies — the check has no applicability rule
KSIA-MEC-076.proof: Certificate within 12 months covering the whole sprinkler network, with noted defects closed.

KSIA-MEC-077.why: Operating a hydrant valve, unreeling a hose and checking access is unobstructed are all done on the equipment.
gaps: INTERVAL CONFLICT: the check says annual flow/pressure tests; ACSA requires valve station flow and pressure tests MONTHLY
KSIA-MEC-077.split: keep signage and unobstructed access, which nothing else covers; the tests are MEC-071/072/074
KSIA-MEC-077.proof: Test tag on each hydrant within date, the valve turning smoothly without excessive force and not leaking at the gland, hose reels unreeled with the isolating valve free and the hose sound, signage present and access unobstructed — plus valve station flow and pressure tests at the MONTHLY interval ACSA requires, not annually.

KSIA-MEC-078.why: Six hours at load is a duration and a load figure in a log. 'Ran OK' is the failure and only the log shows it.
KSIA-MEC-078.proof: Quarterly log stating the actual load or pressure achieved and a full six-hour duration, with any alarm or fault recorded.

KSIA-MEC-079.why: The record must show a simulated failure, not a manual switch. Only its description distinguishes them.
KSIA-MEC-079.proof: Monthly record of a genuine simulated pressure-loss or power-failure changeover, stating the changeover time against the design starting time.

KSIA-MEC-080.why: State of charge and starting capability are measured. The walk's contribution is checking BOTH batteries of a dual set were tested.
KSIA-MEC-080.proof: Monthly log per battery — both of a dual set — with a result, and a replacement following any marginal result.

KSIA-MEC-081.why: The gauge on the wall gives today's reading; the log gives the series. The check is the two agreeing, against the design values.
KSIA-MEC-081.proof: Weekly pressure and level log against fire-engineering design values, the gauge itself verified accurate, and a repeatedly low reading investigated rather than logged.

KSIA-MEC-082.why: A charger test and a battery test are routinely conflated into one entry. Only the record shows whether the charger was actually exercised.
gaps: overlaps MEC-080 in practice — the two are commonly recorded as one test
KSIA-MEC-082.proof: A monthly record that names the charger test distinctly from the battery test and confirms correct float-charging.

KSIA-MEC-083.why: Locked and sealed open is a physical state of a valve. You look at the padlock.
KSIA-MEC-083.proof: Suction and discharge valves found locked or sealed in the open position, free to operate and not seized, with the monthly exercising record.

KSIA-MEC-084.why: Level against the minimum runtime in the design basis. The walk reads the tank and checks fuel quality was actually looked at, not assumed.
KSIA-MEC-084.proof: Weekly level log with the reserve meeting the design runtime, and evidence that water contamination and diesel bug were checked, not just the level.

KSIA-MEC-085.why: A roll-up of the seven pump-station checks above.
gaps: introduces two terms — 'churn test' and 'jockey pump' — that appear nowhere else in the register and have no ACSA threshold
KSIA-MEC-085.split: delete the duplicated halves; keep the churn test and the jockey pump as their own checks IF ACSA's manual actually requires them, which needs confirming first
KSIA-MEC-085.proof: Weekly pressure gauge, water level and diesel level logs; monthly battery, charger, valve and electric-to-diesel switch-over tests; the quarterly six-hour diesel full-load run per SANS 10287 cl. 10.1 with the load achieved recorded; and tank levels against design. NOTE: 'churn test' and 'jockey pump' appear nowhere in ACSA's manual — confirm they are required before auditing against them.

KSIA-MEC-086.why: A calibration certificate against a serial number, plus daily bump tests. The walk proves the certificate belongs to the monitor actually carried into the sump.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — no gas monitor calibration interval is stated
KSIA-MEC-086.proof: Calibration certificate matching the serial number of the unit in field use, daily bump-test records before each entry, and the monitor configured for H2S, LEL and O2.

KSIA-MEC-087.why: A measured trip current and time in a test record.
gaps: fifth of six near-identical earth-leakage rows: MEC-012, 052, 064, 087, 092, 102
KSIA-MEC-087.split: one earth-leakage check scoped by asset system

KSIA-MEC-088.why: A guard is fitted or it is lying beside the pump. That is seen.
KSIA-MEC-088.proof: Every coupling and shaft guarded, guards undamaged and reinstated after maintenance access, grid covers in place with their limit switches working.

KSIA-MEC-089.why: Two checks in one — diagram and CoC — for the pump control panel.
gaps: duplicates MEC-010 and MEC-009 scoped to a different panel; the same pair recurs at MEC-052, 064, 094 and 101
KSIA-MEC-089.split: one wiring-diagram-and-CoC check scoped by asset system

KSIA-MEC-090.why: Duty/standby setting, balanced run hours and a float switch fouled with rag are read at the panel and in the wet well.
KSIA-MEC-090.proof: Duty/standby alternating with roughly balanced run hours, level sensors clean and free, alarms confirmed through to IMC on the monthly cycle, standby power proven, and spill history with each event investigated.

KSIA-MEC-091.why: Read as written it is the same gas-monitor certificate check as MEC-086.
gaps: WRONG SYSTEM: the requirement, evidence and walkabout all say SEWER SUMP and confined-space entry, filed under Gas Hot Water Facility. This is a copy of MEC-086 pasted into the wrong asset system.
if a gas monitor is genuinely required at a gas hot water facility it would be for LPG/combustible gas, which is a different instrument and a different configuration from H2S/LEL/O2
KSIA-MEC-091.split: delete, or rewrite as an LPG gas-detection check and confirm against ACSA's hot water system task list first

KSIA-MEC-092.why: As MEC-087, scoped to the gas hot water facility.
gaps: sixth of six near-identical earth-leakage rows
KSIA-MEC-092.split: one earth-leakage check scoped by asset system

KSIA-MEC-093.why: A fitted guard is seen. But this row's evidence describes PUMP couplings and shafts.
gaps: evidence text says 'pump couplings, shafts' — copied from MEC-088 (Sewer Pumps) without re-scoping to what actually rotates in a gas hot water facility
the acsaThreshold cited is from Air Handling Units (D080 025M cl. 4.4.5), a third unrelated system
KSIA-MEC-093.split: rewrite against the approved contractor task list for System - Hot Water (HWS) rather than inheriting the pump text

KSIA-MEC-094.why: As MEC-089, scoped to the gas hot water facility panel.
gaps: fifth of five near-identical wiring-diagram-and-CoC rows
KSIA-MEC-094.split: one wiring-diagram-and-CoC check scoped by asset system

KSIA-MEC-095.why: A CoC from a registered LPG installer, plus leak test records. Ventilation, signage and cylinder storage are the visible half.
gaps: this is the ONLY substantive check in the Gas Hot Water Facility system — the other four (091-094) are copy-pastes from other systems
KSIA-MEC-095.proof: LPG installation CoC naming a registered installer, leak test records, ventilation openings unobstructed, signage present, cylinders stored upright, secured and segregated, with the flammable store designed to SANS 10400 and SDS held close by.

KSIA-MEC-096.why: An HBA reg 7 monitoring programme with results. The walk finds the staff rotated into exposure who were never scoped into it.
KSIA-MEC-096.proof: Documented monitoring programme with the procedure used and results, an OREP per homogeneous exposure group, covering every role actually exposed — including recent rotations.

KSIA-MEC-097.why: Not whether a procedure exists but whether decontamination is actually done and whether every disposal produced a manifest. The gap between the procedure and the practice is the check.
KSIA-MEC-097.proof: Written decontamination and waste-handling procedures, a manifest and safe-disposal certificate for EVERY disposal in the period reconciled against the waste register, from a site with a current permit — and visible evidence decontamination is performed on equipment.

KSIA-MEC-098.why: A clause in a signed contract. The walk checks the party on site is the party in the contract.
KSIA-MEC-098.proof: Signed contract carrying the HBA reg 17(f) clause and EMS 048 appended and signed before commencement, with the personnel actually working matching the contracted entity.

KSIA-MEC-099.why: The hierarchy of control is a way of working. PPE issued but not worn, and a ventilation cover left off, both fail it while the register says compliant.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — the control hierarchy has no stated criterion here
KSIA-MEC-099.proof: Risk assessment, PPE of the correct grade for biological hazard actually available and in use, engineering controls in place and maintained, and hygiene facilities usable — with issue and inspection registers behind them.

KSIA-MEC-100.why: An HBA reg 12(b) examination report by an approved inspection authority. The walk checks the report's scope covers every control installed.
KSIA-MEC-100.proof: Thorough examination report within 24 months, listing each engineering control — with nothing installed on site missing from its scope.

KSIA-MEC-101.why: As MEC-089, scoped to the water treatment plant.
gaps: fourth of five near-identical wiring-diagram-and-CoC rows
KSIA-MEC-101.split: one wiring-diagram-and-CoC check scoped by asset system

KSIA-MEC-102.why: As MEC-087, scoped to the water treatment plant.
KSIA-MEC-102.split: one earth-leakage check scoped by asset system

KSIA-MEC-103.why: Bund capacity against what is actually stored, and incompatible chemicals sharing a shelf, are both seen in the store.
KSIA-MEC-103.proof: Bunding at least 110% of the largest container in it, SDS present and matching the chemicals actually held, ventilation and signage in place, and incompatibles segregated.

KSIA-MEC-104.why: A sign is on a wall or it is not, and it either names the right protection or it does not.
KSIA-MEC-104.proof: Signage present, legible and specifying the required hearing protection in every area the AIA survey put at or above 85 dBA — including areas added or changed since that survey.

KSIA-MEC-105.why: The same AIA noise survey as MEC-016.
gaps: verbatim duplicate of MEC-016 — identical requirement, evidence and walkabout
KSIA-MEC-105.split: delete; one site noise survey check, with demarcation as MEC-104

KSIA-MEC-106.why: SANS 241 is a laboratory schedule. A chlorine residual can be spot-read at a tap, but the compliance is the monthly series.
KSIA-MEC-106.proof: Monthly sampling and test results at FALE against the SANS 241 schedule, disinfection residuals within range, reservoir cleaning records — and sampling points on site that show signs of routine use.

KSIA-MEC-107.why: A DMR reg 18.6 thorough examination by a competent person from a registered entity. Rope and hook wear is visible, but the report's itemisation is the check.
KSIA-MEC-107.proof: Six-monthly report itemising ropes, chains, hooks, sheaves, brakes and safety devices individually — not a generic pass — from a registered Lifting Machinery Entity.

KSIA-MEC-108.why: A load test certificate is read against the SWL stamped on the machine. Both halves are needed.
KSIA-MEC-108.proof: Certificate within 12 months stating a test load consistent with the SWL nameplate, from an ECSA-registered inspector at a registered entity — both verifiable, not merely claimed.

KSIA-MEC-109.why: Pre-use checklists exist to be filled in before use. Batch-completed at month end they are a record of nothing, and only the dates and their storage location reveal that.
KSIA-MEC-109.proof: Completed checklists stored at the equipment, dated and timed one per use occasion, covering controls, safety devices, anchor points and harness attachment — with no evidence of retrospective batch completion.

KSIA-MEC-110.why: A register is compliant when it matches the equipment on site in both directions — nothing decommissioned still listed, nothing new missing.
KSIA-MEC-110.proof: Register listing each item with its SWL and last/next examination and load-test dates, reconciled both ways against the identification tags found on site.

KSIA-MEC-111.why: A DMR reg 19 registration is a document. The walk checks the entity doing the work is the entity registered, not a sub-contractor.
KSIA-MEC-111.proof: Current DoL Lifting Machinery Entity registration for the entity actually performing the load tests, with SHE File competencies submitted 14 days before work.

KSIA-MEC-112.why: An individual's ECSA registration under the Engineering Profession Act, plus their employment by a registered entity. Neither is observable on site.
gaps: no walkabout text at all, correctly
KSIA-MEC-112.proof: ECSA registration for the named inspector and evidence they are employed by the registered Lifting Machinery Entity that issued the certificates.

KSIA-MEC-113.why: A roll-up of MEC-107, 108 and 110, adding operator competency.
KSIA-MEC-113.split: keep only operator competency, which nothing else asks, and the displayed-tag check on cradles, hoists, MEWPs and lifting tackle
KSIA-MEC-113.proof: A load-test certificate within twelve months displayed on or near each cradle, hoist and MEWP and matching the unit, issued by an ECSA-registered LMI at a DoL-registered Lifting Machinery Entity; a lifting tackle register with a valid inspection tag or colour code on each sling and shackle at the three-monthly cycle; and operator competency evidenced on the training register.

KSIA-CIV-001.why: The paint on the ground IS the check. A repaint log proves work happened, not that the marking is visible today.
KSIA-CIV-001.proof: Every marking type legible at taxi/approach speed, no rubber, fuel, dust or vegetation obscuring it — plus the monthly inspection report and the CMMS repaint interval actually applied to each marking type.

KSIA-CIV-002.why: A measured stripe/gap against the approved as-built. Neither half decides it alone — the drawing without the tape measures nothing, the tape without the drawing has no standard.
gaps: no acsaThreshold — D060 009M defers dimensions to ICAO Annex 14 and the as-builts, so the figure lives in a drawing this register does not name
KSIA-CIV-002.proof: Measured centre-line stripe/gap, TDZ pair count and spacing within tolerance of the approved as-built for THIS runway, and the as-built current for the declared distances in force.

KSIA-CIV-003.why: Visibility is a condition of the asset. Nothing in a file can make a faded marking compliant.
gaps: overlaps CIV-001 almost entirely — 001 is 'conspicuous condition', 003 is 'visibility'

KSIA-CIV-004.why: Colour is read off the pavement. The paint spec says what was bought, not what is on the ground after two years of jet blast.
KSIA-CIV-004.proof: White/yellow/red as prescribed per marking type, apron safety lines still contrasting against stand markings, mandatory markings true red — not faded to pink.

KSIA-CIV-005.why: A holding-position distance is a measurement against the approved design, not against a textbook figure.
KSIA-CIV-005.proof: Surveyed or measured distance from runway centre line to each holding position equal to the approved design/AIP figure — and the as-built updated if the runway has been re-declared.

KSIA-CIV-006.why: Same physical reading as 002/003/004, narrowed to mandatory instruction markings — where a fade is a runway incursion rather than an untidiness.
gaps: bundles four attributes (visibility, dimensions, colour, background) into one pass/fail
KSIA-CIV-006.split: keep as one — mandatory markings warrant their own check, but say in the requirement that it is the mandatory subset of 002/003/004

KSIA-CIV-007.why: A roll-up of 001-006 plus the repainting programme. Nothing here is verified that is not verified above.
KSIA-CIV-007.split: delete the condition half; keep only 'repainting programme exists and the interval per marking type is being met', which is a Document check
KSIA-CIV-007.proof: A repainting programme in the CMMS showing the interval applied to EACH marking type — centre line monthly, runway edges bi-annually — worked to date, obstacles repainted tri-monthly, monthly inspection reports determining removal and repainting, and a retro-reflectivity reading where the equipment exists. Condition itself is CIV-001 to CIV-006.

KSIA-CIV-008.why: Word-for-word CIV-001, filed under Visual Aids instead of Markings.
gaps: exact duplicate of CIV-001 — same requirement text, same evidenceExpected, same walkabout

KSIA-CIV-009.why: Apron markings read on the stand, against the stand's design drawing and the aircraft type actually parking there.
KSIA-CIV-009.proof: Markings visible and correctly coloured, and lead-in/lead-out lines matching the aircraft type currently using the stand — a stand upgauged to a wide-body with the old lines still painted is the failure this catches.

KSIA-CIV-010.why: A sign is present, oriented and lit, or it is not. All three are seen.
gaps: conflicting threshold in the source: signage inspection Daily (D060 001M cl. 4.9.23) versus Monthly (D060 014M cl. 4.7.8)
KSIA-CIV-010.proof: Each mandatory sign present, red/white, panel undamaged, oriented for the direction of travel, and illuminated where the runway operates at night or below 800 m RVR.

KSIA-CIV-011.why: Frangibility and siting are physical. The obstacle survey behind it is a document, and that is the half that is not seen.
gaps: bundles four unrelated asset types — signs, PAPI, wind indicators, obstacle marking/lighting — plus a document (the obstacle survey)
KSIA-CIV-011.split: split four ways: PAPI siting and frangibility (Asset); signs (already CIV-010); wind indicators (already CIV-012); obstacle survey currency within the 10 km radius (Document)
KSIA-CIV-011.proof: Signs and PAPI sited as the design layout shows, the PAPI structure and its mounts of frangible break-away design, the annual PAPI flight calibration certificate current, wind indicators and obstruction lights checked daily, and a Technical Evaluation under D060 015M current for the 10 km radius with WGS-84 three-dimensional coordinates and SA-CAA approval correspondence for anything erected.

KSIA-CIV-012.why: A windsock is judged by watching it move and by what stands between it and the pilot.
KSIA-CIV-012.proof: Sock the correct size, not torn or faded, swinging freely, lit if required, grass at its base under 20 cm, and no new structure or tree in the line of sight or disturbing the airflow.

KSIA-CIV-013.why: A rut is found by walking on it with a straightedge. The condition survey says where to look.
KSIA-CIV-013.proof: No depression, hump or rut in the touchdown or high-turn areas that a straightedge shows outside tolerance, and every irregularity in the latest PCI survey either closed or carrying a live work order.

KSIA-CIV-014.why: Bearing strength cannot be seen. The published PCR decides it; the walk only checks that the traffic on the pavement is the traffic the PCR was calculated for.
KSIA-CIV-014.proof: Current PCR report in the five-part coded format, and no aircraft type in the actual movement mix with an ACR above it.

KSIA-CIV-015.why: RESA is ground you can walk. Whether there is enough of it is a measurement against the declared distances.
KSIA-CIV-015.proof: Measured RESA length and width at each end meeting the figure in the declared-distance calculation, clear of encroaching objects, standing water and uneven ground.

KSIA-CIV-016.why: Cracking, rutting, depression and shoving are seen and severity-rated on the pavement.
gaps: overlaps CIV-025, which asks the same question with the PCI survey as its evidence
KSIA-CIV-016.proof: No conspicuous distress on the pavement that is absent from the latest survey, and the survey itself within its three-yearly cycle.

KSIA-CIV-017.why: Ponding, loose aggregate and vegetation in joints are transient conditions — a record of a clean surface last month proves nothing about today.
KSIA-CIV-017.proof: No area meeting the standing-water definition after rain, no loose aggregate that could become FOD, and no vegetation in joints beyond the 30 cm herbicide band.

KSIA-CIV-018.why: A lip at the pavement edge is felt underfoot and measured with a straightedge.
gaps: no threshold anywhere in the source for how big a step is a failure — the check has no pass mark
KSIA-CIV-018.proof: No measurable step between pavement and shoulder at representative points — and, first, a documented tolerance to measure against.

KSIA-CIV-019.why: Crumbling asphalt at the edge is seen, and the fragments are the FOD source.
gaps: overlaps CIV-016 (surface defects) and CIV-018 (edge flush) — three checks walking the same 10 cm of pavement
KSIA-CIV-019.split: fold into CIV-018 as the edge check

KSIA-CIV-020.why: A longitudinal slope is not judgeable by eye. The as-built or survey profile decides; the walk only finds local flat spots and reverse grades at patches.
KSIA-CIV-020.proof: Current survey profile within the code-based longitudinal and transverse limits, and no localised reverse grade at a joint or patch holding water.

KSIA-CIV-021.why: The graded strip is walked and compared against the design width; encroachment is the failure and it is visible.
KSIA-CIV-021.proof: Graded extent matching the design drawing for the runway's code number, grass under 20 cm across the 50 m band, and no fencing, drainage or service road inside the graded width.

KSIA-CIV-022.why: Strip bearing capacity is a geotechnical number. The walk can only find seasonal softness a dry-season CBR would miss.
gaps: no acsaThreshold and no ACSA evidence named at all — the CBR figure and the RFF trafficability standard are not in the register
KSIA-CIV-022.proof: CBR results or a geotechnical report for the graded strip showing it will carry an RFF vehicle, and ground visibly firm at the time of the audit.

KSIA-CIV-023.why: Every object in the strip is counted on the ground and matched to a register that says it is frangibly mounted. An unregistered object is the finding.
gaps: two different checks in one: frangibility of authorised objects, and the presence of unauthorised ones
KSIA-CIV-023.split: split in two — frangible-mount certification of every registered object (Asset/reconcile), and a clear-strip sweep for unauthorised objects (Asset/examine)

KSIA-CIV-024.why: A friction coefficient cannot be seen. The signed CFME report is the only thing that decides it; rubber build-up in the touchdown zone is a hint, not a reading.
gaps: evidence stub: 'Friction test reports; action records'
KSIA-CIV-024.proof: Signed friction results for RWY 06/24 at the three-monthly interval, tested at 1 mm self-wetting with a smooth tread tyre, every section above the maintenance planning level — or a corrective-action record where it was not.

KSIA-CIV-025.why: The PCI survey is the instrument; the walk cross-checks it. But 016, 017 and 019 already walk the same defects.
KSIA-CIV-025.split: keep as the document check — 'PCI survey current within 3 years and every distress it records carries a programmed repair' — and let 016/017/019 carry the condition
KSIA-CIV-025.proof: A PCI survey to ASTM D5340 within the three-yearly cycle, every distress it records carrying a programmed repair or a closed work order, concrete apron joint material replaced on the five-yearly cycle, and nothing visibly serious on the pavement that is absent from the survey.

KSIA-CIV-026.why: Same instrument, same report, same decision as CIV-024.
gaps: duplicates CIV-024 — one is under Runway/Friction, the other under its own asset system

KSIA-CIV-027.why: Movement statistics against Table A's traffic ladder. Purely a reconciliation of two records — nothing on the airfield changes the answer.
gaps: no walkabout text at all, correctly
KSIA-CIV-027.proof: Average daily turbo-jet arrivals per runway end, the Table A band that number falls in, and test dates showing that interval actually applied — plus a Z001 003M change record if traffic moved the band.

KSIA-CIV-028.why: The existence and completeness of the record register is the check.
gaps: no walkabout text at all, correctly
overlaps CIV-024, whose evidence is the same reports
KSIA-CIV-028.proof: Register covering 2-3 years with date, runway end, device and tyre, measured Mu by section, and the corrective-action reference — each signed off within two weeks and retained five years.

KSIA-CIV-029.why: Not whether a report exists but whether a below-threshold reading actually PRODUCES rubber removal, a re-test and, at minimum level, a NOTAM. That loop either runs or it does not.
KSIA-CIV-029.proof: For each reading at or below the maintenance planning level, a corrective work order, the treatment record, and a post-treatment re-test above the level — and for any at or below minimum, the NOTAM.

KSIA-CIV-030.why: Same physical reading as CIV-013, on the taxiway.
gaps: identical requirement text to CIV-013 and CIV-039 — the register repeats the pavement condition set once per surface type
KSIA-CIV-030.split: consider one pavement-condition check scoped to a surface, rather than three identical checks

KSIA-CIV-031.why: As CIV-014, for the taxiway. The PCR decides; the walk notes push-back and turning areas the evaluation must have allowed for.
gaps: requirement asserts 'taxiway strength to be equal to that of runways' with no source named for that rule
KSIA-CIV-031.proof: Taxiway-specific PCR report and no ACR in the using traffic above it.

KSIA-CIV-032.why: Same physical reading as CIV-016, on the taxiway.
gaps: walkabout text says 'Walk the runway' — copied from CIV-016 and not re-scoped

KSIA-CIV-033.why: Same transient condition as CIV-017, on the taxiway.

KSIA-CIV-034.why: A step at the taxiway/apron junction is where construction dates meet; it is found on foot.
gaps: no threshold for the size of a failing step, same as CIV-018

KSIA-CIV-035.why: Same as CIV-019, on the taxiway.

KSIA-CIV-036.why: Whether the slope drains is answered by looking at the taxiway after rain — unlike the runway's longitudinal profile, this one IS visible.
KSIA-CIV-036.proof: No ponding after rainfall; where there is ponding on a design-compliant cross-section, a downstream blockage identified and a work order raised within the same operational day.

KSIA-CIV-037.why: As CIV-021, for the taxiway strip against its code letter.

KSIA-CIV-038.why: A roll-up of 030-037 with nothing new in it.
gaps: duplicates CIV-030, 032, 034, 035 and the taxiway centreline marking is already CIV-001/003
KSIA-CIV-038.proof: Monthly taxiway and taxilane inspection plus the three-yearly visual assessment, manoeuvring areas inspected at least three times a week, concrete joint material replaced five-yearly, and no unsafe condition on the walk — one that could affect aircraft handling or generate FOD — that is not already recorded against a specific check.

KSIA-CIV-039.why: Same physical reading as CIV-013, on the apron.

KSIA-CIV-040.why: As CIV-014, for the apron — with the added point that a stand carries a static load a rolling evaluation may not cover.
KSIA-CIV-040.proof: Apron PCR report whose method accounts for static parking loads, and no stand routinely taking an aircraft heavier than its rating.

KSIA-CIV-041.why: Same physical reading as CIV-016, on the apron.
gaps: walkabout text says 'Walk the runway' — copied from CIV-016 and not re-scoped

KSIA-CIV-042.why: Same transient condition as CIV-017, on the apron.

KSIA-CIV-043.why: The apron edge meets four different surrounding types and each boundary is walked.

KSIA-CIV-044.why: A corner break is a triangular crack in a concrete slab — the one distress on this register that is genuinely apron-specific and not a repeat.
KSIA-CIV-044.proof: No corner break or failed joint sealant absent from the survey, and concrete joint material replaced on the five-yearly cycle.

KSIA-CIV-045.why: Fuel staining and a broken grounding point are seen on the stand. But the spill-response procedure bundled in with them is a practice, and the separator test is a document.
gaps: three different check types in one: surface condition (Asset), spill clean-up procedure (Practice), tie-down and grounding point condition (Asset)
KSIA-CIV-045.split: split the spill-response half out as a Practice check — 2-hour containment, disposal records retained 5 years — and leave condition and grounding points as the Asset check
KSIA-CIV-045.proof: Stand pavement sound with joint sealant intact, no fuel or oil staining, tie-down rings and aircraft grounding points present, unbroken and uncorroded — plus a spill response procedure with containment inside 2 hours, oil separators tested annually for efficiency, sludge depth under 25% of chamber depth and disposal records retained 5 years.

KSIA-CIV-046.why: Whether a reassessment was TRIGGERED is a document question; the walk only establishes that works happened that should have triggered it.
KSIA-CIV-046.proof: For every major repair or construction in the period, a post-works PCR reassessment, a pre-return-to-service friction verification, and the updated figure submitted to the AIP.

KSIA-CIV-047.why: The published rating and the evaluation behind it are documents; the walk notes whether real traffic still matches.
gaps: says PCN, which ICAO replaced with PCR — the register is on the old vocabulary here while CIV-014 uses PCR
KSIA-CIV-047.split: merge into CIV-014, keeping only the overload-approval control as its own line
KSIA-CIV-047.proof: A published pavement strength rating supported by a current evaluation and matching the AIP entry, with a controlled approval on file for every overload operation. NOTE: the check says PCN, which ICAO replaced with PCR — read it as the PCR published under CIV-014.

KSIA-CIV-048.why: The requirement is 'as rapidly as possible' — a response time, not a condition. The build-up you see is evidence the practice is not running.
KSIA-CIV-048.proof: Removal log showing elapsed time from detection to completion against the friction trigger, the method used, and a post-treatment friction result back above the maintenance planning level.

KSIA-CIV-049.why: FOD is cleared continuously or not at all; a clean runway on audit day proves the sweep ran this morning, nothing more. The programme and its coverage are the check.
KSIA-CIV-049.proof: FOD Management Programme document, sweep log covering runway, taxiway AND apron with location, date, time and nature of each item, bins inspected twice daily and emptied at three-quarters, and FOD in induction training records.

KSIA-CIV-050.why: A blocked catchpit is seen by lifting the lid. Silt and vegetation are conditions of the asset.
KSIA-CIV-050.proof: No visible blockage in accessible drains, catchpits and culvert outlets; the cleaning schedule covering every airside drainage asset group; and blocked inlets on a runway or taxiway closed within 2 hours.

KSIA-CIV-051.why: The drains are the same drains as CIV-050. The separator servicing bundled in is a document check with a laboratory result behind it.
gaps: duplicates CIV-050 for the drains; overlaps CIV-017/033/042 for the ponding
KSIA-CIV-051.split: keep only the oil/water separator half and make it a Document check — annual efficiency test, sludge depth under 25% of chamber depth, disposal records retained 5 years
KSIA-CIV-051.proof: Stormwater drains, culverts and channels clear of silt, debris and vegetation with an inspection register covering every airside drainage asset group; oil/water separators tested annually for efficiency with sludge depth under 25% of chamber depth and hazardous waste disposal at a licensed facility recorded and retained 5 years; and no ponding on any movement area.

KSIA-CIV-052.why: Not whether a log exists but whether the rounds actually happen at the stated frequency — which is why the walkabout says shadow one.
KSIA-CIV-052.proof: Three logged manoeuvring-area inspections every day with no unexplained gap, the apron audit twice a month, the bay inspection daily during turnaround, and the most recent annual inspection signed by a qualified civil engineer.

KSIA-CIV-053.why: The existence of a written programme and procedure, with responsibilities and defect-correction timeframes named in it.
gaps: no walkabout text at all, correctly
KSIA-CIV-053.proof: The documented inspection programme and procedure in the Aerodrome Manual or SMS, naming who inspects what at what interval and the timeframe for correcting each defect priority.

KSIA-CIV-054.why: Whether defects raised in the log are actually closed on the ground. That closure loop is the practice.
gaps: duplicates CIV-052 for the daily inspection frequency
KSIA-CIV-054.split: keep only the defect-closure loop; the frequency is CIV-052
