KSIA-CIV-054.proof: A daily movement-area serviceability log with today's entry present, checklists forwarded daily to the responsible Manager and audited by them, every defect raised carrying an Oracle eAM work request with a Date of Call, and the recent defects visibly fixed or in progress on site — plus wildlife and FOD reports for the period.

KSIA-CIV-055.why: Road surface, joints, signage and markings are all read on the road.
gaps: bundles pavement condition, signage and markings — the same three the runway gets as separate checks
KSIA-CIV-055.proof: Road pavement and expansion joints sound, signage present and legible, vehicle control markings visible — and the specific locations from the March 2025 finding actually repaired.

KSIA-CIV-056.why: A hole in a fence is seen. The patrol records bundled in are a separate, document-shaped question.
gaps: bundles fence condition (Asset), clear zones (Asset), patrol records (Document) and gate/access-control function (Asset)
KSIA-CIV-056.split: split the patrol and inspection record half out as a Document check — weekly gate checks, monthly condition monitoring, fence voltage tests against the design range
KSIA-CIV-056.proof: Perimeter fence with no holes, gaps, sagging or corroded sections and nothing climbable against it; clear zone free of vegetation and stored materials, perimeter grass under 20 cm across the 3 m band; weekly gate visual checks and monthly condition monitoring records; fence voltage tests within the site design range; and a sample gate and access-control point observed working.

KSIA-BFM-001.why: A per-building certificate register; the walk compares current use and layout to what the register says the building is.

KSIA-BFM-002.why: The original Certificate of Occupancy and any plan-approval for changes; the walk finds retail units or extensions the CoC does not cover.

KSIA-BFM-003.why: Current electrical CoC from a registered person; the walk looks for a new DB or tenant fit-out wiring not covered by a supplementary CoC.

KSIA-BFM-004.why: Form 4 plus a fire compliance certificate within 12 months; the walk reads extinguisher, sprinkler and emergency-lighting tags for current dates.

KSIA-BFM-005.why: Form 4 for the structural system with the engineer's ECSA registration; the walk finds visible alterations lacking updated certification.

KSIA-BFM-006.why: Occupancy, fire, electrical and lift certificates current.
KSIA-BFM-006.split: four certificate families with four different issuers and intervals in one row
KSIA-BFM-006.proof: An occupancy certificate describing the building's CURRENT use and layout, local-authority fire compliance current, an electrical Certificate of Compliance per building in the latest SANS 10142-1 format with its test report and not older than two years, and current lift/escalator certificates — all accounted for in the yearly COC reconciliation across the BDG, SBD, TRF and LGT asset groups.

KSIA-BFM-007.why: Corrosion, cracking, delamination, spalling, exposed reinforcement. The survey report records the condition; the concrete IS the condition.

KSIA-BFM-008.why: Visible cracking, staining, leaking on structure and facades.

KSIA-BFM-009.why: Settlement and deflection, read off crack-width monitors and level-survey points at the structure.

KSIA-BFM-010.why: Ponding, loose sheeting, blocked downpipes, failed waterproofing.
KSIA-BFM-010.proof: Roof sheeting sound and fixed, gutters, drop boxes and downpipes clear and undamaged, waterproofing intact with no bubbling, cracking or lifted membrane, no ponding on the roof, and no ceiling water damage left unrepaired — against three-monthly roof/gutter/drop box inspections and monthly ceiling, walkway and canopy inspections, with a work order raised for each defect.

KSIA-BFM-011.why: Approved drainage plans and confirmation of the municipal connection or approved on-site system; the walk traces the connection point to the plan.

KSIA-BFM-012.why: Approved drawings, design reports and O&M manuals, with where they are version-controlled.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether they are accessible to the SITE team or only at head office — that is a different test from whether they exist

KSIA-BFM-013.why: Traps and vents correctly installed and in condition, and odour at the outlets. Odour is not a documentary fact.

KSIA-BFM-014.why: Scheduled-versus-actual servicing dates for grease traps, vent stacks and sumps; the walk looks for buildup and overflow staining that contradict the log.

KSIA-BFM-015.why: Trade-effluent discharge consent and meter/desludging logs; the walk confirms the meters and sumps are present and functional.

KSIA-BFM-016.why: Drain test certificates dated and signed off before the pipework was covered. Nothing is visible now — that is the point of the record.

KSIA-BFM-017.why: Tests whether a job card marked completed means the work was done. Sample a closed card and look for the repaired item on site.

KSIA-BFM-018.why: The requirement is that suitable means EXIST — channels, pipes, outlets present, functional and matching the plan.

KSIA-BFM-019.why: Sight each component for damage, disconnection or infilling.

KSIA-BFM-020.why: The seasonal schedule and completed job cards; the walk finds debris that should have been cleared before the season.

KSIA-BFM-021.why: Tests whether the programme is run — accumulated silt against a schedule that says it was cleared is the finding.

KSIA-BFM-022.why: A manhole paved over or silted up cannot be inspected, whatever the drawing shows.

KSIA-BFM-023.why: SANS 241 test certificates; the walk checks non-potable outlets carry legible marking.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether the supply is municipal or ACSA-operated — the sampling obligation differs completely

KSIA-BFM-024.why: Measured outlet temperature, sewer odour in ablutions, fixtures functional.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether ACSA has a defined temperature standard at all
KSIA-BFM-024.proof: Hot water measured at the outlet within the design range, no persistent drain or sewer odour in ablutions, backflow prevention devices fitted and tested where required, leaks found and closed out on the monthly water reticulation inspection, and ablution fixtures working — with the two-hourly signed ablution sheet countersigned and the weekly B&FM audit on file.

KSIA-BFM-025.why: Impervious surfaces, vermin protection present and intact.

KSIA-BFM-026.why: Sight the area against the drawings, and look for informal collection points that are not on any drawing.
KSIA-BFM-026.proof: A refuse storage area that exists on the ground where the approved drawings show it, listed in the Register of On-Site Waste Stores EMS 111, with AEMR written approval for any temporary or stakeholder-controlled area, and NO informal collection point that has grown up outside the register. NOTE: ACSA prescribes no area, volume or number — the compliance test is registration and approval, not size.

KSIA-BFM-027.why: Bins sealed, odour on approach, active pest control visible.

KSIA-BFM-028.why: The contract or municipal schedule and three months of waybills; overflowing bins on the walk contradict them.

KSIA-BFM-029.why: The collection route unobstructed and not running through passenger or food-service areas.

KSIA-BFM-030.why: Cleanliness, spillage, overflow, and recycling separation infrastructure actually in use.
KSIA-BFM-030.split: hygiene (Asset), contractor licensing (Document) and pest control in one row
KSIA-BFM-030.proof: Waste areas clean, with no spillage or overflow; labelled recycling and general bins actually in use, not merely present; a Waste Register EMS 112 whose generated, disposed and recycled quantities reconcile; a manifest and safe disposal certificate for every removal, from a contractor whose receiving site permit is on file; and pest control records. All retained five years.

KSIA-BFM-031.why: Rust staining, coating breakdown, bare steel on canopies, cladding and PLB gantries.
KSIA-BFM-031.proof: Structural steel, canopy soffits, cladding supports and PLB gantries with corrosion protection intact — no rust staining, coating breakdown or bare steel — against three-monthly roof and gutter rust checks and monthly canopy, walkway and paint checks, with a repainting programme whose frequency is justified by the inspection reports, and the March 2025 finding locations actually repaired.

KSIA-BFM-032.why: Torn or missing sealant, damaged cover plates.
KSIA-BFM-032.proof: Movement and expansion joint sealants intact — not torn, perished or missing — cover plates present and secure, with no water ingress or trip hazard, across terminal floors, walkways and parkade decks and ramps. Three-monthly wall expansion observations and the yearly PLB fixed-tunnel expansion joint check on record. NOTE: ACSA states no sealant type or joint gap tolerance.

KSIA-BFM-033.why: Cracked or chipped panels, perished seals, loose fixings.
KSIA-BFM-033.proof: Curtain wall and glazing panels uncracked and unchipped and of safety glass where required, seals unperished and gap-free, fixings and brackets tight and uncorroded — checked monthly and three-monthly — plus a façade inspection programme, and any cleaning above 1.7 m done by a certified height contractor with an approved Safety File and FALE proof of training at height.

KSIA-BFM-034.why: Floor damage and slipperiness near entrances and wet areas, damaged ceilings, housekeeping.
KSIA-BFM-034.proof: Floors undamaged and slip-resistant, especially at entrances and wet areas; ceilings without missing tiles or water staining; doors, finishes and furniture safe; housekeeping to the QMS 85% monthly cleanliness benchmark and FALE's ASQ rating of 4.2, with helpdesk logs evidencing the 5-minute response and 15-minute correction the FALE SLA requires.

KSIA-BFM-035.why: Ramp gradients, accessible lifts in service, accessible ablutions unlocked and not used for storage.
KSIA-BFM-035.proof: Ramps at a usable gradient and unobstructed, accessible lifts in service, accessible ablutions unlocked, working and not used for storage, the disabled lift alarm button at 900-1200 mm; way-finding legible and consistent with the Wayfinding Signage Design Manual; and statutory safety signage plus exit indication present and lit, with escape routes checked clear daily.

KSIA-BFM-036.why: Tests whether the daily checklist is really completed daily and whether its entries match what is on the ground.

KSIA-BFM-037.why: Tests whether 'closed' means done, and whether a long-open card has a live defect behind it.

KSIA-BFM-038.why: Tests whether claimed PM completion is real, by spot-checking assets the CMMS says were recently serviced.
KSIA-BFM-038.proof: A building maintenance plan in Oracle eAM with PM work orders executed within the 14-day or 7-day window, a backlog report scored against that window, condition grading against D060 026M's six hazards, and — the actual test — a sample of assets marked 'PM completed' showing the work is evident on site.

KSIA-EDM-001.why: A distribution licence/supply agreement. Nothing on site can make it compliant.

KSIA-EDM-002.why: The agreement's SCOPE decides it — does it authorise reselling to tenants. The question reads the document, it does not replace it.
KSIA-EDM-002.proof: The authority or licence to distribute and resell electricity to tenants, and the distribution agreement with the municipality, read for SCOPE — does it actually authorise reselling — plus tenant lease agreements carrying the energy efficiency requirements and a metering schedule showing every kiosk ready board and distribution board on the electronic metering system.

KSIA-EDM-003.why: Calibration certificate within 5 years is the pass/fail. The walk reads the meter's tag and seal to prove the certificate is THIS meter's.

KSIA-EDM-006.why: NRS 057 intervals evidenced by certificates and the register; the walk matches tags and CT/VT nameplate ratios to what is recorded.
KSIA-EDM-006.proof: Calibration certificates for every bulk and tenant meter held by the Electrical Maintenance Department, calibration tags on the meters matching the register, CT/VT nameplate ratios matching what is recorded and programmed for that meter, and a transformer routine test report evidencing the CT ratio and polarity check. NOTE: ACSA states no calibration interval — NRS 057 supplies it.

KSIA-EDM-007.why: Tests whether reconciliation actually CATCHES everything — an unbilled supply is found by walking the site, not by reading the reconciliation that omits it.
gaps: evidence stub: 'Bills vs meter data reconciliation'
KSIA-EDM-007.proof: A reconciliation of every metering point and intake substation on site against the municipal bills, with the tariff category confirmed correct for the demand profile, and NO supply found on the walk — a newer building, a generator, a tenant connection — that has no corresponding municipal account. This is kick-off risk item 6.5.1 and an unbilled premium supply is found by walking, not by reading the reconciliation that omits it.

KSIA-EDM-008.why: The kWh figures and % change are the proof; the walk confirms the claimed initiatives physically exist and run.

KSIA-EDM-009.why: A documented target and the actual Rand saving with its calculation basis.

KSIA-EDM-010.why: Prior and current figures with the methodology.

KSIA-EDM-011.why: Monthly records and KPIs against targets; the walk confirms the dashboards those reports cite are live.
KSIA-EDM-011.proof: Monthly consumption records for KSIA with kWh/pax and kWh/m² tracked against a stated target, hourly energy-use model data per asset, system, process or area, BMS out-of-range alerts raised as CMMS energy audit job cards, and the dashboards the reports cite live and showing current data on the walk.

KSIA-EDM-012.why: Interval demand data against the registered NMD, plus any penalty notices.

KSIA-EDM-013.why: Tests whether the peak/load-shed strategy is real — equipment configured AND control-room staff able to say how a peak is managed.
KSIA-EDM-013.split: NMD compliance (a figure) and demand-management practice are two different tests in one row
KSIA-EDM-013.proof: Interval demand data showing maximum demand never exceeding the registered Notified Maximum Demand, municipal accounts checked for exceedance penalties, and a peak/load-shed strategy that physically exists — demand-limiting configured in the BMS, generator or load-shed triggers installed — with control-room staff able to describe what happens as a peak approaches. NOTE: ACSA states no NMD figure or penalty rule.

KSIA-EDM-014.why: Service report within 12 months is the pass/fail; the walk checks service tag, cleanliness, damage, fault indicators.

KSIA-EDM-015.why: SCADA irradiance-vs-output data is the proof; the walk checks the pyranometer is clean and correctly positioned, because a dirty sensor invalidates the data.

KSIA-EDM-016.why: PR reports monthly and rolling annual; the walk looks for soiling, shading and damaged panels that explain a low PR.

KSIA-EDM-017.why: THE CLEANEST ASSET CASE HERE. Shadow on panels. No document can establish it — you stand there and look, at the right time of day.
KSIA-EDM-017.proof: No shadow falling on any panel from trees, structures or equipment at the time of the visit — checked early morning or late afternoon when shadows are longest — and string-level monitoring showing no string persistently underperforming its neighbours, which is shading the eye missed.

KSIA-EDM-018.why: CoC and maintenance/cleaning records; the walk checks soiling, inverter ventilation clearance and cable labelling.
KSIA-EDM-018.split: PR monitoring, maintenance records, CoC and earthing/lightning protection are four tests in one row
KSIA-EDM-018.proof: Performance ratio monitored on a live system, inverter and panel cleaning and maintenance records, a PV installation Certificate of Compliance in the latest SANS 10142-1 format with its test report and not older than two years, and earthing and lightning protection test results. NOTE: the earthing results are not required by any ACSA clause found — they must be requested.

KSIA-EDM-019.why: Four separate approvals — grid connection, land rights, environmental, wheeling. The question establishes which apply, not whether they exist.
KSIA-EDM-019.split: four approval types, four different authorities

KSIA-EDM-020.why: Ventilation unobstructed, detector heads present and undamaged, isolation switches labelled and accessible. The battery room's state decides.
KSIA-EDM-020.proof: Ventilation louvres and fans unobstructed and running, fire detection heads present, undamaged and in service tag date, gas suppression maintained yearly with cylinders inside the 10-yearly hydrostatic test, isolation switches located and labelled, manufacturer maintenance current, and the room inside 0-40 °C and 20-80% RH. NOTE: D118MAN cl. 8.6 requires lithium-ion for UPS batteries.

KSIA-EDM-021.why: Plant left in manual override and aged unresolved alarms are a practice failure, not a document failure. The BMS screen is where you see it.
KSIA-EDM-021.proof: No plant left in manual or hand override, the active alarm list free of unresolved or aged alarms, set-points and schedules matching what the plant is actually doing on site, car park lighting at 100% on presence and 40% on absence, motion sensor timeouts configured as specified, and BMS out-of-range alerts converted to CMMS energy audit job cards.

KSIA-EDM-022.why: Green Star certificate with rating level and validity.

KSIA-EDM-023.why: Water supply agreement, tariff schedule, invoices matching the agreed tariff.

KSIA-EDM-024.why: Tests whether a leak-detection programme is actually run — walking pipework for damp patches and pooling is how you find out.
KSIA-EDM-024.proof: Bulk and sub-meters functional and readable, monthly or quarterly consumption recorded, a continual leak investigation programme with walkabout records for leaking tanks and pipelines, monthly water reticulation inspections covering meter operation, rain and grey-water use where installed, and the Register of Effluent and Storm Water Discharge Points EMS 105 current.

KSIA-EDM-025.why: The LTO emissions inventory against ICAO 9889 methodology; the walk confirms the ambient monitoring station that feeds it is installed, calibrated and running.

KSIA-EDM-026.why: Emissions report with reduction targets tracked.
KSIA-EDM-026.proof: Carbon footprint calculations for KSIA against a stated boundary and methodology, the ACI Airport Carbon Accreditation certificate, environmental objectives and targets set under the KSIA EMS with review records, and the reduction trend in the Integrated Annual Report — supported by the annual EMS peer-review audit and the ISO 14001 certification cycle.

KSIA-PSR-001.why: HIRA reviewed annually and a maintained register is the pass/fail; the walk spot-checks that listed controls physically exist as described.
KSIA-PSR-001.proof: A site HIRA to B170 001M using the 25-cell Severity A-E × Likelihood 1-5 matrix, reviewed annually or after any change or incident, with the eight-column ICAO SMM log carrying both the initial (column 6) and residual (column 8) Safety Risk Index, controls and named owners against each risk, evidence of all five B170 cl. 4.1 triggers, HIRA reports submitted to the SACAA Director of Civil Aviation — and 2-3 listed controls confirmed to physically exist on site as described.

KSIA-PSR-002.why: Tests whether change control happens BEFORE implementation. A current abnormal configuration that never went through MOC is the failure, and only asking finds it.
KSIA-PSR-002.proof: An Engineering Asset Modification Request M&E 088 for every change, a change record in the Asset Modification Register for every request INCLUDING rejected ones, the five sequential D060 020M stages evidenced in order (each a prerequisite of the next), the ten mandatory steps for tenant-initiated modifications, a formal HIRA before each named trigger, and Asset Modification Committee minutes approving it before implementation.

KSIA-PSR-003.why: A control 'verified in place and effective' is settled by finding the bonding, the lockout point, the fall-arrest anchor. The register listing it proves nothing.
KSIA-PSR-003.proof: A control physically checked per top risk area — fuel: overfill and bonding protection; electrical: a lockout/isolation point; heights: fall-arrest anchors and edge protection; airside vehicles: speed control — each traceable to the Compliance Risk Management Plan GOV 006 with all nine mandatory fields including residual rating, responsibility and target date, and the residual band matched to the mandated strategy (Avoidance / Reduction / Segregation of exposure).

KSIA-PSR-004.why: Cracked bund walls and water in hydrant pits fail this whatever the paperwork says.
KSIA-PSR-004.split: MHI notification and risk assessment (Document) sit in the same row as bund and pit-lid condition (Asset) — two different failures, one row
gaps: evidence stub: 'MHI RA; emergency plan; inspection'
KSIA-PSR-004.proof: MHI notification on site with signage, an AIA risk assessment within five years, an emergency plan tested within twelve months and submitted to NERSA annually, bund walls uncracked and the bund dry with its drain valve closed, and hydrant pit lids sitting flush with no water pooling — water in a pit is both the ingress and the contamination route this check exists for.

KSIA-PSR-005.why: Hazardous-area classification drawings and Ex inspection records; the walk matches Ex markings and tags on fittings to the classified zones on the drawing.
KSIA-PSR-005.proof: Hazardous-area classification drawings covering the fuel farm, hydrant pits AND generator rooms, current for the plant as built, with electrical fittings in every classified zone carrying a visible Ex marking at or above the zone's requirement and a current inspection tag. NOTE: the register names no ACSA evidence for this check — the drawings must be requested by name.
gaps: evidence stub: "HAC drawings; Ex inspection records"

KSIA-PSR-006.why: Spill kits present, complete and in date; separator not full of oil. Presence is a physical fact.
KSIA-PSR-006.split: spill equipment condition, separator servicing and drill records are three tests
KSIA-PSR-006.proof: Spill kits at the fuel farm and at every fuelling position, sealed, complete and in date; oil/water separators with a service tag, tested annually for efficiency, sludge depth under 25% of chamber depth and not full of oil or debris; spill drills recorded; and a spillage report logged with the Helpdesk for every environmental incident, with containment inside the 2-hour limit and safe disposal certificates retained 5 years.

KSIA-PSR-007.why: The fire cut-out present, labelled and accessible; the tank bunded and separated. Nothing documentary settles it.
KSIA-PSR-007.proof: A fire cut-out or isolation point in each generator room, present, labelled and accessible; the diesel tank separated from the generator and bunded to at least 110% of the largest container; fire extinguishers present, in date and unobstructed; and the weekly off-load and monthly on-load test records evidencing the fuel shut-off valve check.

KSIA-PSR-008.why: Bund condition, visible separation, dispensing containment.
KSIA-PSR-008.split: tank certification is a Document test inside an Asset row
KSIA-PSR-008.proof: Bulk diesel tank with a certification plate, permits on file for above and underground tanks, a bund that is empty, uncracked and drain-valve-closed at at least 110% of the biggest container, visible fire separation from the generator, a contained dispensing point with access control, and the tank entered on the Register of Dangerous Goods EMS 109.

KSIA-PSR-009.why: A current plan and recorded drills are the proof; the walk confirms the assembly points and equipment the plan NAMES are actually there and unobstructed.
KSIA-PSR-009.proof: A current aerodrome emergency plan, evacuation and emergency drills held and recorded within period, the Fuel Depot plan tested at least every twelve months with the practice-test records kept, Emergency Co-ordinator, Evacuation Officer and Fire Warden appointments in writing and inside their three-year validity — and the assembly points, signage and equipment the plan names actually present, visible and unobstructed on site.

KSIA-PSR-010.why: Eyewash flows, first-aid box stocked and in date, extinguisher gauge in the green. The inspection register records it; the equipment decides it.
KSIA-PSR-010.proof: Emergency showers and eyewash with a current tag, water flowing and unobstructed; first-aid boxes stocked and in date at the ratio the headcount requires (one trained first aider per fifty employees, at least one per working environment, appointed on OHS 004 with a current certificate from a DoL-registered provider); spill kits sealed and complete; fire equipment in date, gauge in the green and unobstructed; assembly points signed.

KSIA-PSR-011.why: Tests whether investigations actually feed the HIRA and whether an action marked 'closed' was really done — the walk verifies one physical corrective action.
KSIA-PSR-011.proof: Incident and near-miss investigations that visibly change something — the HIRA updated, a maintenance regime changed, a recurring failure mode (generator, fuel pit) trended — with preliminary reports inside 7 days, full reports inside one month, Annexure 1 submitted to the DoL where required, and any corrective action involving a physical change confirmed implemented on site.

KSIA-PSR-012.why: Fire doors propped open and blocked escape routes are the failure. The FRA is context.
KSIA-PSR-012.split: fire risk assessment and marshal appointments (Document) vs compartmentation and escape routes (Asset)
KSIA-PSR-012.proof: A current fire risk assessment; fire doors that close fully and are not propped; compartmentation intact; escape routes and fire equipment unobstructed; exit signage visible and lit with daily escape-route clearance checks; the yearly record of Fire Hazard Classes per occupancy to SANS 10400-T; council-approved designs validated yearly; and Fire Warden appointments in writing, inside their three-year validity and on the OHS Appointments Register.

KSIA-PSR-013.why: Hydrant markers visible and accessible, pump room condition, access routes not blocked by vehicles.
KSIA-PSR-013.proof: A fire-water assessment showing storage, pump capacity and hydrant coverage adequate for the terminal, fuel farm and plant rooms; hydrant markers and covers visible and accessible; the pump room sound with its weekly and monthly test records complete and the quarterly six-hour full-load run done; and fire-service access routes clear of vehicles, materials and parked equipment.

KSIA-PSR-014.why: A permit system exists on paper everywhere. The test is a live permit during the audit and whether the controls it lists — fire watch, gas testing, barricading — are actually in place.
KSIA-PSR-014.proof: A permit-to-work system covering hot work, confined space, electrical isolation and working at heights, permits signed by BOTH parties at issue AND at cancellation, gas testing results recorded on the permit face, a fire watch held at least 30 minutes after hot work with the area inspected at one hour and monitored a further three, permits audited, and any live permit on site matching the controls actually in place.

KSIA-PSR-015.why: Flammables away from oxidisers, ventilation working, SDS physically AT the store rather than filed centrally.
KSIA-PSR-015.split: inventory and LPG CoCs (Document) vs storage segregation and ventilation (Asset)
KSIA-PSR-015.proof: A hazardous chemical inventory classified to SANS 10228, SDS physically accessible at the store rather than filed centrally, storage segregated (flammables away from oxidisers), ventilated and signed, bunding at at least 110% of the biggest container, LPG installations certified, an Asbestos Register EMS 103, and confined-space and hot-work procedures approved by the GMR 2(1) and 2(7) appointees.

KSIA-PSR-016.why: Cylinders upright, chained, segregated by gas type, empty and full separated. A clean single-subject Asset check.
KSIA-PSR-016.proof: Cylinders upright, chained or strapped, segregated by gas type, in a ventilated and signed area, with empty and full clearly separated; Written Safe Work Procedures for compressed gas cylinders approved by the GMR 2(1) and 2(7) appointees; the Pressure Equipment Regulations register with three-yearly inspection and test; and SCBA cylinders at 300 bar and never below 80% of filling pressure, hydrostatically tested at least every 4 years.

KSIA-PSR-017.why: A signed, dated GMR 2(1) letter and competency certificate; the walk confirms the named appointee is the person actually doing it, via records bearing their name.

KSIA-PSR-018.why: Monthly visit records unbroken, 6-monthly rope and 12-monthly safety-gear entries present; the walk reads the unit's own on-site register.

KSIA-PSR-019.why: The National Artisan Certificate itself, not an attendance letter; matched to the person doing millwright work.

KSIA-PSR-020.why: Contractor SAQCC Fire registration and service records; the walk reads service tags for a legible in-interval date.

KSIA-PSR-021.why: Current CoC and its test report, issuer registered; the walk checks it covers visible subsequent additions.

KSIA-PSR-022.why: Flight-check certificate and calibration records; the walk confirms the localizer and glide path equipment is present, powered, undamaged and free of interference.

KSIA-PSR-023.why: The trade test certificate for the electrical trade specifically, matched to the person doing the work.

KSIA-PSR-024.why: Two adjacent lights out is an ICAO failure you find by driving the runway at night. The outage log records it; the runway decides it.
KSIA-PSR-024.split: AGL outage limits (Asset) and standby changeover records (Document) in one row

KSIA-PSR-025.why: The question is the crux: does servicing include actual detector-head functional testing, or only panel and battery checks. A full service record of the wrong service is still non-compliant.

KSIA-PSR-026.why: A Water Use Licence or documented General Authorisation basis; the walk identifies the actual discharge points and matches them to what is authorised.

KSIA-PSR-027.why: Friction test reports against the applicable minimum, at the frequency for that runway's traffic, with the device's calibration certificate. All desk work.

KSIA-PSR-028.why: Register reviewed within 24 months with ACM locations on floor plans; the walk confirms warning labels are where the register says.

KSIA-PSR-029.why: A workplace plan, if one is still maintained.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether this requirement is still live at all — it may be obsolete

KSIA-PSR-030.why: Provisional. The row does not say what it tests.
gaps: the row's own question asks what this line is meant to test — ISO 14001, an internal policy, or something else. It cannot be audited as written.
KSIA-PSR-030.proof: Evidence for whatever 'Sustainability' is being tested — GBCSA certification at the 4 Star minimum, the business case with IRR, NPV, profitability index and payback, the 36-month maintenance schedule, FMEA and RAM studies, and operations and maintenance competency records against D100MAN cl. 4's targets (99.5% availability, 20-year design life, power factor 0.95, >40% saving on retrofits). NOTE: the requirement is a single word and is not an appointment or a competency — it does not belong in this asset system.

KSIA-PSR-031.why: Board-approved policy, current register, committee minutes evidencing review.
gaps: the row's own question asks whether this is enterprise risk management or plant-level OHS risk assessment — two different auditees

KSIA-PSR-032.why: ISO 55001 documents if alignment is claimed, otherwise planned preventive maintenance records.
gaps: the row's own question asks which of the two it is — the evidence required differs completely

KSIA-PSR-033.why: The renewal programme and its capital linkage; the finding is a visibly deteriorated asset that does NOT appear on it.

KSIA-PSR-034.why: Appointment letters current with competency evidence; the walk confirms the named person is the one performing the role.
KSIA-PSR-034.split: GMR 2(1), 16(2), EIR/EMR and LI/LMI are four separate statutory appointments in one row
KSIA-PSR-034.proof: Written appointments for GMR 2(1) on OHS 008, GMR 2(7) on OHS 009, Section 16(2) on OHS 001, supervisors on OHS 002 and the electrical EIR/EMR and LI/LMI roles, each inside its three-year validity, carrying all four mandatory content elements, with the competency evidence the role requires — at or above 11kV the GMR 2(1) appointee needs a recognised Engineering Qualification AND the legislative training — and the named person actually performing the role, evidenced by inspection, SOP or permit records bearing their name.

KSIA-PSR-035.why: Training matrix and rosters; the walk spot-checks staff doing height, gas or electrical work against a current matching competency.
KSIA-PSR-035.proof: A training matrix completed with the Line Manager covering trade tests, wireman's licence, LPG and working at heights, with OHS induction inside 30 days of commencing work, on-the-job training inside 30 days of employment or transfer, GMR 2(1) and 2(7) legislative training inside 6 months of appointment; standby rosters and call-out records; and a sample of staff doing height, gas or electrical work on site holding a current matching competency.

KSIA-PSR-036.why: Tests whether the arrangement holds — is work stopped when a s37(2) agreement lapses, do inductions expire. The filed agreement proves only that one was signed.
KSIA-PSR-036.proof: A Section 37(2) mandatary agreement OHS 040 for every contractor on site, a SHE File submitted at least 14 days before commencement and reviewed within 7 working days scoring at least 90% on OHS 037 for high-risk work, permit-to-work and hot-work permits for the work actually in progress, induction records — and the contractor teams observed on site matching the names on the filed agreements.

KSIA-PSR-037.why: Ask maintenance staff how they report a near-miss and check those examples are in the register. A mismatch is the finding, and no document shows it.
KSIA-PSR-037.proof: An incident register with near-misses in it, notification inside ACSA's clock (12 hours for a fatality, 24 hours for a Section 24 injury or LTI, 36 hours for Section 24(c) equipment failure, 72 hours for a near miss), Annexure 1 submitted to the DoL, investigations closed with their corrective actions, and a trend review. The real test is asking maintenance staff how they report a near-miss and finding the examples they describe in the register.
